newsitem.title: USA: US W.COAST SPOT GASOLINE STAYS FIRM IN THIN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: US W.COAST SPOT GASOLINE STAYS FIRM IN THIN MARKET.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot gasoline prices rose Wednesday with buyers scrambling to cover their shipping commitments for the second week of August, dealers said.
CARB unleaded gasoline traded between 77 cents and 78 cents a gallon Wednesday, up two cents from Tuesday and continuing a sharp rise that began early last week when gasoline was 63 cents.
"People are still trying to cover first and second cycle," a refinery trader said.

A key inventory report late Tuesday confirmed market sentiment that high volumes of exports and agricultural demand have depleted stocks the last month. American Petroleum Institute showed West Coast supply down 947,000 barrels last week.
Inventories on the West Coast have fallen to almost four million under year-ago levels, API reported.
Gasoline for delivery the second week, or second cycle, of August were priced two cents a gallon over end-of-month supplies, when traders see supply replenished by increased production.
In Los Angeles, conventional regular unleaded gasoline rose about 3.00 cents a gallon to 72/73 cents, traders said.
More plentiful supplies of distillates kept prices in check Wednesday, with CARB diesel fuel traded between 67/68.50 cents, flat from Tuesday.
San Francisco products were priced the same as L.A.
